findings.summary: This part teaches the gateway, stitching comparison, operations, and the full worked supergraph (pages 1–8) before it ever defines subgraph anatomy and reference resolvers (pages 9–10), so nearly every earlier page depends on the last two.
findings.evidence: Page 1 already says "Later steps send `_entities` with reps pulled by `Flatten`" and page 8 recaps "Reference resolvers are the join implementation", but page 9 only then states "Federation adds `_service` and `_entities` to every subgraph" / "A representation is just `__typename` plus the key fields", and page 10 gives the first `__resolveReference` definition under "4. Reference Resolver Shape".
findings.fix: Move the two "Run and test in isolation" pages (current pages 9–10: subgraph anatomy, `_service`/`_entities`/`_Entity`/`_Any`, representations, reference resolvers) to the front of this part, ahead of "The Gateway And Query Planning", so the planner pages can refer back to `_entities` and representations instead of forward.

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a series label rather than a hook, so the scroll-stopping line is buried in sentence two.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of GRAPHQL FEDERATION. One endpoint for clients, ten teams shipping independently — that is the whole pitch of GraphQL federation, and the bill arrives in round trips."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and demote the label: "One endpoint for clients, ten teams shipping independently — that is the whole pitch of GraphQL federation, and the bill arrives in round trips. Part 2 of GRAPHQL FEDERATION."

findings.summary: There is no `?dry-run` query-string parameter for getting a query plan — it is the `Apollo-Expose-Query-Plan: dry-run` request header, and it only works when plan exposure is explicitly enabled.
findings.evidence: "`?dry-run` returns the plan without executing"
findings.fix: Replace with: "`Apollo-Expose-Query-Plan: dry-run` header returns the plan without executing (needs `--dev` or `plugins.experimental.expose_query_plan: true`)".

findings.summary: The claim that every non-GraphQL source needs a hand-written subgraph server is outdated — Apollo Connectors (`@source`/`@connect`) map REST APIs into the supergraph declaratively with no subgraph server to own or operate.
findings.evidence: "Federation needs a subgraph shim in front of each" / "That shim is code you must own and operate" / "Stitching wins outright for legacy and third-party"
findings.fix: Add a bullet: "REST sources need no shim — Apollo Connectors (`@source`/`@connect`) declare them in schema; gRPC/SOAP still need one." and soften the QA to "stitching or Connectors win for legacy and third-party".

findings.summary: The cross-boundary N+1 is described as N HTTP fetches, but the router always collapses one plan step's representations into a single `_entities` request — contradicting this page's own later bullet.
findings.evidence: "N+1 crosses the boundary: 100 products, 100 reviews fetches" vs. later on the same page "`_entities` already batches keys into one plan step"
findings.fix: Rewrite as "One `_entities` call carries 100 representations — the N+1 is inside the subgraph, 100 DB round trips" and change the next bullet to "DataLoader inside the resolver is what avoids it".

findings.summary: Connector lines in the Test pyramid flowchart run straight through the "subgraph resolvers" and "_entities calls" boxes, striking through their text.
findings.evidence: Edges b1->c1_0 and b3->c3_0 in post.json are routed as long verticals that cross the intervening single-column rows; in the render a line passes horizontally through the middle of the words "subgraph resolvers" and "_entities calls".
findings.fix: Route the long edges around the single-node rows (offset the vertical segments outside the box bounds), or restructure the flowchart so each branch has its own column instead of stacking c0_0..c3_0 in one centre column.

findings.summary: Stating that borrowed key fields must carry `@external` is Federation 1 guidance; Federation 2 (which the rest of the part assumes, e.g. `@override(from:)`) does not require it on `@key` fields.
findings.evidence: "Borrowed key fields carry `@external`, nothing more", and the SDL on pages 2 and 5: "type User @key(fields: \"id\") {", "  id: ID! @external"
findings.fix: Change the bullet to "In Federation 2 the borrowed key field is declared plainly — `@external` is only needed for `@requires`/`@provides`" and drop `@external` from the `id: ID!` lines in the page 2 and page 5 SDL blocks.

findings.summary: `rover dev` does not run your subgraph servers; it starts only a local router and composes against subgraph endpoints or schema files you supply.
findings.evidence: "`rover dev` runs router plus subgraphs locally"
findings.fix: Change to "`rover dev` runs a local router against subgraphs you start yourself (local or remote endpoints)".

findings.summary: `_entities` (and the `_Entity` union) is added only to subgraphs that declare at least one `@key` type, not to every subgraph.
